texts: Surgical intervention for discrete valvar aortic stenosis is indicated when the echocardiographic mean gradient is >40 mm Hg: A.
In children the usual threshold is a mean gradient above 40 mm Hg (or a peak gradient around 60 to 70 mm Hg), or less if there are symptoms, ischaemia on the ECG or falling ventricular function.
A gradient of 25 mm Hg, or hypertrophy alone, calls for follow-up rather than intervention, and mixed stenosis and regurgitation is weighed case by case.
In the picture, Franky reaches for his tools only when the gauge across the stone mouth reads above 40.
Memory hook: forty on the gauge, and the tools come out.
